questions.stem: A private subnet's route table directs 0.0.0.0/0 to which target for outbound internet?
questions.explanation: Private subnets reach the internet via a NAT Gateway in a public subnet. IGW would make the subnet public; peering is VPC-to-VPC.

questions.stem: Security groups are:
choices: Stateless and have explicit Deny rules
questions.explanation: SGs are stateful (return traffic is auto-allowed) and only support allow rules. NACLs are stateless and subnet-scoped.

questions.stem: How many IPs does AWS reserve in every subnet?
questions.explanation: AWS reserves the first 4 IPs and the last IP in each subnet, regardless of size.

questions.stem: What is the scope of an Availability Zone?
choices: One or more data centres with independent power and network, within a Region
questions.explanation: An AZ is a logically isolated group of one or more DCs in the same Region with independent failure domains.

questions.stem: A NAT Gateway is:
choices: AZ-scoped, deploy one per AZ for HA
questions.explanation: NAT Gateways live in a specific AZ; HA requires one per AZ so a single-AZ failure doesn't cut off other AZs.

questions.stem: An Internet Gateway differs from a NAT Gateway because:
choices: IGW is inbound+outbound and used by public subnets; NAT is outbound-only for private subnets
questions.explanation: IGW enables full bidirectional internet access for resources with public IPs; NAT lets private-subnet resources egress while remaining unreachable from the internet.

questions.stem: Which VPC endpoint type is free and only available for S3 and DynamoDB?
questions.explanation: Gateway endpoints are routed via the route table and free; interface endpoints (PrivateLink) cost per hour and per GB.

questions.stem: VPC peering is:
choices: Transitive: A↔B and B↔C means A can talk to C
Non-transitive: only the two peered VPCs can communicate
questions.explanation: Peering is non-transitive. Use Transit Gateway when you need many VPCs to interconnect.

questions.stem: An NACL rule is evaluated:
choices: Numbered rules in order, first match wins
questions.explanation: NACLs evaluate rules by rule number, lowest first; the first match (allow or deny) wins.

questions.stem: An ALB needs to be public-facing. Where should it sit?
questions.explanation: A public ALB requires public subnets in multiple AZs (with a route to IGW) for HA.

questions.stem: A 'local' route in a VPC route table:
choices: Can be deleted to isolate subnets
Is implicit and cannot be removed; covers VPC CIDR traffic
questions.explanation: Every route table has an implicit local route for the VPC CIDR that you cannot delete.

questions.stem: Which service is the AWS DNS and traffic-routing service?
questions.explanation: Route 53 is the authoritative DNS service with multiple routing policies.

questions.stem: Which Route 53 routing policy routes users to the lowest-latency Region?
questions.explanation: Latency-based routing selects the endpoint that gives the lowest measured latency to the client.

questions.stem: Which AWS service replaces a mesh of VPC peerings with a hub-and-spoke topology?
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway is the hub for many VPCs and on-prem networks; it scales beyond what pairwise peerings can manage.

questions.stem: Which connection option provides a dedicated fibre link from on-prem into AWS?
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provisions a physical cross-connect at a DX location for predictable high bandwidth.

questions.stem: Which is the IPv6 equivalent of NAT for private subnet egress?
questions.explanation: Because IPv6 addresses are globally unique, AWS provides an Egress-Only IGW that allows outbound-only IPv6 traffic.

questions.stem: A 3-tier VPC needs HA across 3 AZs. How many NAT Gateways are recommended?
questions.explanation: NAT Gateways are AZ-scoped; one per AZ prevents an AZ outage from cutting off another AZ's egress.

questions.stem: Reaching S3 from a private subnet without going through the public internet is achieved by:
choices: NAT Gateway with S3 IP allow-list
questions.explanation: An S3 Gateway endpoint adds a route to S3 prefix-list, keeping traffic on the AWS backbone and saving NAT cost.

questions.stem: A security group rule references another security group as source. This means:
choices: Only resources with that other SG attached are allowed
All traffic from the VPC is allowed
Only the same SG self-reference is allowed
questions.explanation: Referencing an SG as source allows traffic from any ENI that has that SG attached — a clean way to chain tiers.

questions.stem: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is best used to:
choices: Expose a VPC service privately to other VPCs/accounts
questions.explanation: PrivateLink lets a provider expose an NLB-backed service privately to consumer VPCs without peering or going via the internet.

questions.stem: An NACL is stateless. What is the implication?
choices: You only need an inbound rule
You must explicitly allow return traffic in the opposite direction
questions.explanation: Stateless means the NACL doesn't remember outbound flows; you must add inbound rules for return traffic on ephemeral ports.

questions.stem: Which CIDR is reserved by RFC 1918 and commonly used for VPCs?
What does the IP 169.254.169.254 refer to inside an EC2 instance?
questions.explanation: 169.254.169.254 is the link-local address of the EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDS).

questions.stem: An RDS instance should typically be placed in:
choices: A public subnet with an IGW route
A private/isolated subnet, reachable only from app SGs
questions.explanation: Databases should never be exposed to the internet; place them in private subnets with SG ingress only from the app tier.

questions.stem: Which feature would you use to allow on-prem servers to communicate privately with multiple VPCs through a single attachment?
choices: Transit Gateway with Direct Connect Gateway
questions.explanation: TGW + Direct Connect Gateway lets one on-prem DX attachment reach many VPCs through the central hub.
